constants.name: input
constants.doc: The puzzle input, with its final newline stripped.

constants.name: Up
constants.doc: Direction: one row up. Points are `(row, col)`.

constants.name: Dirs4
constants.doc: The 4 directions, clockwise from up. `Dirs4[(i + 1) % 4]` turns right.

constants.name: Dirs8
constants.doc: The 8 directions (with diagonals), clockwise from up.

functions.name: panic
functions.doc: Stops the program with an error message.

functions.name: print
functions.doc: Prints to stderr, for debugging. *(reference interpreter extra)*

functions.name: min
functions.doc: The smaller of two values of the same type (ints, chars, strings, tuples, lists).

functions.name: max
functions.doc: The larger of two values of the same type (ints, chars, strings, tuples, lists): `best = max(best, x)`.

functions.name: abs
functions.doc: Absolute value: `abs(r1 - r2) + abs(c1 - c2)`. Traps on `int::Min`.

functions.name: pow
functions.sig: pow(base: int, exp: int, mod = m?) -> int
functions.doc: `base` to the power `exp` (not negative); traps on overflow. With `mod = m`: modular exponentiation, result in `0..m`, never overflows.

functions.name: Set
functions.doc: A new set, empty or with one element. From a collection: `xs.to_set()`.

functions.name: Map
functions.doc: A new map. With `default`, missing keys read as `v`, so `counts[k] += 1` works. Without it, a missing key traps.

functions.name: Queue
functions.doc: First in, first out. `push(x)`; `pop()` is a maybe-value.

functions.name: MinQueue
functions.doc: Priority queue, lowest priority first. `push(item, priority)`; `pop()` gives `(item, priority)`.

functions.name: Grid
functions.doc: A new grid filled with one value.

functions.name: file
functions.doc: Reads a file next to the program, for `test file("example.txt") == …`.

methods.name: lines
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the lines, without `\n` / `\r\n`.

methods.name: ints
methods.doc: Lazy chain of every integer in the text. `-` is a sign only right before a digit and not after one: `"x=-2"` → -2, `"2-4"` → 2, 4.

methods.name: digits
methods.doc: Lazy chain of every digit char as an int, skipping everything else.

methods.name: digits
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the decimal digits, most significant first (sign ignored).

methods.name: chars
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the chars. (A string can also be iterated directly.)

methods.name: split
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the parts between separators. `input.split("\n\n")` gives the blank-line sections.

methods.name: split_once
methods.doc: The parts before and after the first `sep`. Traps if there is none.

methods.name: int
methods.doc: Parses the whole string as an int; traps on anything else. To pull numbers out of text, use `ints()`.

methods.name: starts_with
methods.doc: Does `prefix` occur at position `at`?

methods.name: to_char_grid
methods.doc: One char per cell. Lines must have equal length.

methods.name: to_digit_grid
methods.doc: One digit 0–9 per cell.

methods.name: to_string
methods.doc: Text form. A grid gives its rows joined with `\n`.

methods.name: digit
methods.doc: `'7'` → 7. Traps on non-digits.

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: `^ > v <` or `U R D L` → `Up` / `Right` / `Down` / `Left`.

methods.name: len
methods.on: string · list · Set · Map · Queue · Stack · MinQueue
methods.doc: Number of elements.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.doc: No elements?

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Adds an element (end of a list, back of a queue, top of a stack).

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Adds an item; the lowest priority pops first.

methods.name: pop
methods.doc: Removes and returns the next element (a MinQueue gives `(item, priority)`). **Maybe-value**: use `while x = q.pop():`.

methods.name: push_all
methods.doc: Pushes every element of a list or chain, in order.

methods.name: pop_many
methods.doc: Removes the top `n`, returned bottom to top. `a.push_all(b.pop_many(n))` moves a block in order.

methods.name: top
methods.doc: The top element without removing it. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: Adds `x`; true if it wasn't there yet. `if !seen.add(p): continue`.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Removes an element / key; true if it was there.

methods.name: keys
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the keys (no defined order). *(reference interpreter extra)*

methods.name: values
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the values (no defined order). *(reference interpreter extra)*

methods.name: sort
methods.doc: Sorts the list **in place**. Use `to_sorted` to get a new list.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc: Number of rows.

methods.name: cols
methods.doc: Number of columns.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: Position of the first matching cell, row by row. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: find_last
methods.doc: Position of the last matching cell. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: positions
methods.doc: Lazy chain of all points, row by row.

methods.name: neighbors4
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the in-bounds neighbors in `Dirs4` order.

methods.name: neighbors8
methods.doc: Lazy chain of the in-bounds neighbors in `Dirs8` order.

methods.name: print
methods.doc: Prints the grid (to stderr), for debugging.

methods.name: map
methods.doc: Lazy: transforms each element.

methods.name: filter
methods.doc: Lazy: keeps the elements where the lambda is true.

methods.name: flat_map
methods.doc: Lazy: each element becomes several.

methods.name: enumerate
methods.doc: Lazy: pairs `(index, element)`.

methods.name: zip
methods.doc: Pairs elements in order: `a.zip(b).map((x, y) => …)`. Lazy. `other` is a chain, list, range or string. Traps if the lengths differ (use `enumerate()` to number elements).

methods.name: scan
methods.doc: Lazy: each running value of the accumulator (`init` itself is not yielded).

methods.name: take
methods.doc: Lazy: the first `n` elements; stops pulling after them.

methods.name: skip
methods.doc: Lazy: everything after the first `n`.

methods.name: rev
methods.doc: Lazy: reverse order. Not available after map/filter/…

methods.name: sum
methods.doc: Adds all elements (0 when empty). Works on points too.

methods.name: product
methods.doc: Multiplies all elements (1 when empty). Ints only; traps on overflow.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: Number of elements; with a char/value, counts equal ones (`s.count('(')`).

methods.name: any
methods.doc: Is it true for some element? Stops at the first.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Is it true for every element? `true` for an empty chain.

methods.name: min
methods.doc: The smallest element (**maybe-value**), or a list of the `n` smallest.

methods.name: max
methods.doc: The largest element (**maybe-value**), or a list of the `n` largest, largest first.

methods.name: first
methods.doc: The first element. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: last
methods.doc: The last element. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: The first element where the lambda is true. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: find_last
methods.doc: The last element where the lambda is true. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: position
methods.doc: 0-based index of the first match. **Maybe-value**.

methods.name: to_list
methods.doc: Collects into a new list.

methods.name: to_set
methods.doc: Collects into a new set.

methods.name: to_map
methods.doc: Collects `(key, value)` pairs into a new map.

methods.name: to_string
methods.doc: Joins chars or strings: `rows.to_string(sep = "\n")`.

methods.name: chunks
methods.doc: Lazy: lists of `n` elements, one group after another (lines 1–3, then 4–6). The last list may be shorter.

methods.name: windows
methods.doc: Lazy: every run of `n` consecutive elements, overlapping (`[1,2,3,4].windows(3)` → `[1,2,3], [2,3,4]`).

methods.name: intersection
methods.doc: Lazy: the elements that are also `in b` (a string, list or Set), keeping order and duplicates. `a.chars().intersection(b).intersection(c).first()`.

methods.name: to_sorted
methods.doc: A new sorted list. `by` gives the key; stable. Tuples, lists and strings compare element by element.
